title: The Story of Guha
intro: This short story about Guha and Lord Rama brings home the point that living with virtue is above everything else one has acquired.
subtitle: Guhan delivers Lord Rama across River Ganga
body: Lord Rama is born as the eldest son of King Dasharatha and Queen Kousalya of Kosala (a kingdom in North India). It is critical to remember that in each Yuga (large period of time), Lord Vishnu is born as a mortal to rid the world of evil and Lord Rama is an incarnation or avatar of Lord Vishnu in Treta Yuga (age). More to come on this during this weekend's story. He is strong-built, skilled with the bow and a symbol of virtue and chivalry. He is called Maryada Purushottam (Perfect Man) who has all the qualities of an ideal man. He marries Princess Sita (an incarnation of Goddess Lakshmi) and is all ready to ascend the throne when fate plays a cruel trick on Him. His father is forced to promise to give the kingdom to His younger brother (Bharatha) and exile Him to 14 years in the forest (to ensure that He does not come back seeking the throne).

Lord Rama believes that carrying out His father’s promise is a son’s duty and he prepares to leave Kosala. His brother, Lakshmana and Princess Sita decide to follow Him anywhere to serve Him. With heavy hearts, the people of Kosala watch the young princes and princess leave the capital in ascetic robes and follow them to the banks of River Ganga. Here, they halt for the night and when the people sleep, Lord Rama calls out to Guha, a boatman. He promises to pay him handsomely to take them across the mighty river Ganga and to stop the sleeping people from following them.

Guha has heard of Lord Rama’s fame. He had heard that once when Rama was walking through a forest, the dust from His feet turned a stone into a woman (broke the curse on a woman stuck in a stone). Guha cracks a joke by offering to wash the dust off Lord Rama’s feet lest more women emerge from rocks on the river bed. Lord Rama smiled for the first time since He left Kosala. Knowing the struggles in store for the royals, Guha with tears streaming down his face, packs the boat with fruits to satisfy their hunger for the next few days and rows the royals across the river.

On getting to the other side, Princess Sita gives Her pearls to Lord Rama to pass on to Guha as payment. Guha refuses to take it saying that people of the same profession don’t pay each other. Lord Rama is perplexed and Guha explains that Lord Rama is also a boatman who helps people across the Sea of Materialism (Samsaara Saagara) to Liberation (Mukti). Guha requested Lord Rama to row him across for free and liberate him from worldly problems when the time came. Lord Rama smiled again and embraced him.

Rama shows us that living with virtue (though it is hard) attracts so many true friends who will stand with us through many adversities. Guha did his duty with devotion and reaped the reward of liberation from the hands of God Himself.
